what: The letter cells of a big wordmark melt and shrink toward the bottom, tied to scroll (1 → .42). They go not from the left but in a droplet-like shuffled order (0, 3, 1, 5, 2, 4), each delayed by .076, for .62 per cell. Swapping from and to makes it grow back in reverse (.05 → 1)

options.to: End vertical scale, default .42 (to make it grow, from: .05; to: 1)
options.order: Delay order (space-separated numbers), default 0 3 1 5 2 4 — repeats if shorter than the cell count
options.dur: Share of each cell that melts, default .62
options.origin: Transform origin of the cell, default 50% 100% (melts into the bottom). Mirror text growing from the top uses 50% 0

use:
TITLE0

· If you split the cells yourself T Plural marker
note: For text-only elements, the part splits the text into cells. The original stretched the text inside each cell vertically and shrank the cells to clip them so the text seemed to melt away. That stretching and clipping is left to the consuming css. With reduced motion the cells are left untouched, so the text stays fully visible.
